body:
Pre-release of the Electron modernization already on master (#79).

## Versions

- Electron 9.4.0 → 45.1.0. Supports macOS Ventura (13) and newer, Windows 10 and newer, and current Linux. Big Sur and Monterey are not supported.
- electron-builder 22.4.0 → 26.18.0
- electron-updater 4.2.4 → 6.8.11
- express 4.17.1 → 4.22.3
- body-parser 1.19.0 → 1.20.9 (direct resolution, and the copy Express pulls in)

## HEVC

Clips are probed with `canPlayType` and `MediaSource.isTypeSupported`. When HEVC cannot be decoded, the desktop window and the server page show a warning and point at the OS player.

Chromium uses the operating-system decoder where one exists: VideoToolbox on macOS, and Media Foundation on Windows when the HEVC Video Extensions are installed. Official Linux Electron builds still cannot decode HEVC. H.264 playback is unchanged. There is no ffmpeg in this app.

## Also in this build

- The folder dialog uses `showOpenDialogSync`, so choosing a drive saves the directory again.
- The renderer runs with context isolation and a preload that exposes only the existing IPC calls.
- Cabin, Track Mode, and Sentry `event.json` are shown. Date-only `RecentClips/YYYY-MM-DD/` folders are included.
- Folder delete uses the selected folder. The on-screen clock follows the playhead.
- Empty or still-growing files return HTTP 416 instead of an unhandled range error.
- The PayPal donate button and its tracking pixel are removed.

Universal macOS zip/dmg targets, explicit context isolation, and the synchronous folder dialog follow the safe parts of #78. That pull request was not merged. Its rewritten history and any signing material were left out.

## Installers

Linux amd64 AppImage and deb are attached when the Linux build succeeds. A Windows NSIS installer is attached only if the Linux cross-compile succeeds.

macOS universal zip and dmg are not attached. Those targets need a Mac (universal binary and hardened runtime). They are still configured in `package.json` for a later Mac build.

Fixed build issues.

Reverted to previous versioning.

Not sure how well this version will hold up :)  It includes a new server-only option, which allows it to run on Raspberry Pi.

It also allows selecting a base folder through the UI (local volume only; the "Open" button should still let you select other drives / volumes).

To start a headless server, clone the repository (or just get the latest source) and do the following...

```
cd teslacam-browser
npm install
node server.js /path/to/TeslaCam
```

...then open a browser on port 8088 (for example http://localhost:8088)

- Fixed skipping that could occur on second playback
- Added "Loading %" indicator
- Now retains date selection after deleting a folder
Fixed "Delete folder".  For reals this time.
Fixed broken Delete and Copy [to clipboard] buttons.

- Improved handling of inconsistent clip lengths.  When one clip is shorter than the others, the clip will be "dimmed" and playback will be delayed as necessary.  This should (hopefully) keep them in sync...
- Added playback speed (1x, 2x, 10x)
- Replaced drop-down time selection with a list of times
Merged “lastFolders” crash PR.

- New "Combined" view shows all videos in a folder on a single timeline
- Bug fixes

- Fixed issue causing seconds on timestamps to be ignored
- Fixed issue preventing videos being shown in the correct order (left, front, right)
- Remembers last used TeslaCam folder location

- Date and time selection moved to collapsible sidebar
- Runs local webserver on port 8088; click the "Browse" button or browse to http://localhost:8088 (Tesla seems to be transitioning to HEVC codec, which external browsers like Safari and Edge may handle better... try it if videos show up blank).
- Now Bootstrap & Vue -based
Minor bugfix to prevent error when cancelling "Open" dialog.

Added "Delete" button: Deletes clips for a specific time interval. Asks for confirmation, and will also remove containing folder if it's empty after clip deletion.

Video elements are now added lazily as the page is scrolled or resized.

Clips can be hidden (and shown again) by clicking the timestamp above them.

This release is functionally identical to 0.0.85, but is now signed for macOS (and possibly Windows).  On macOS, this should make it much easier to run first time (without having to CTRL+open it).  It should also enable auto-updates (so it'll look for updates each time it's opened), but we'll see...
Fixed a silly bug that obscured the top of the first videos (and playback controls).

Attempted to make the video loading lazier.  It seems a little snappier and more reliable.

Added "Copy" buttons, which will copy the file path of selected folder or front camera view to clipboard (for use in other tools such as [tesla_dashcam](https://github.com/ehendrix23/tesla_dashcam) to merge videos).

The date selection / navigation no longer scrolls off the top.

May see some flicker on scroll on larger screens...
Now aggregates RecentClips entries into single dropdown entry (with "Recent" suffix).

Now lets you open any folder from TeslaCam down.

Note auto-update doesn't yet work; hopefully resolved soon.
Another very minor cosmetic improvement (slightly increased margins) and auto-update tweaks.
First version with (hopefully) auto-updating and publishing via GitHub.

name: Initial prototype
body:
First release.  Very rough around the edges with a hideous user experience.

[macOS DMG](http://bobstrogg.no-ip.org/teslacam-browser/dist/teslacam-browser-0.0.1.dmg)
[macOS ZIP](http://bobstrogg.no-ip.org/teslacam-browser/dist/teslacam-browser-0.0.1-mac.zip)
[Windows EXE](http://bobstrogg.no-ip.org/teslacam-browser/dist/teslacam-browser-Setup-0.0.1.exe)
[Linux AppImage](http://bobstrogg.no-ip.org/teslacam-browser/dist/teslacam-browser-0.0.1.AppImage)

When the app starts, it'll pop up a regular folder browser.  Point it to the "SavedClips" folder containing your Sentry Mode & saved Dashcam videos.  That should show a list of dates & times, and selecting one should show the videos inside.  Click the text above each row of videos to start playback (currently there's no pause / stop / scrub controls...  I'm still pretty impressed considering it's only 2 evenings' work ;) ).
